facts.text: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
facts.explanation: Construction began around 1632 in Agra.

facts.text: The Taj Mahal is built mostly from red sandstone.
facts.explanation: It is white Makrana marble. Agra's Red Fort is the red sandstone one.

facts.text: The tiger is India's national animal.
facts.explanation: The Bengal tiger has been the national animal since 1973.

facts.text: The peacock is India's national animal.
facts.explanation: The peacock is the national bird. The tiger is the national animal.

facts.text: The Ganga rises from the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand.
facts.explanation: Its source stream, the Bhagirathi, flows from Gaumukh at the glacier's snout.

facts.text: The Ganga flows into the Arabian Sea.
facts.explanation: It drains into the Bay of Bengal through the Sundarbans delta.

facts.text: India's Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit on its first attempt in 2014.
facts.explanation: India was the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit.

facts.text: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's north pole.
facts.explanation: It landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023.

facts.text: India won the Cricket World Cup in 1983 under Kapil Dev.
facts.explanation: India beat the West Indies at Lord's in the final.

facts.text: India won its first T20 World Cup in 2011.
facts.explanation: India won the first T20 World Cup in 2007. 2011 was the ODI World Cup.

facts.text: Sachin Tendulkar scored 100 international centuries.
facts.explanation: 51 in Tests and 49 in ODIs.

facts.text: Sachin Tendulkar never scored a double century in an ODI.
facts.explanation: He scored the first men's ODI double century, against South Africa in 2010.

facts.text: An octopus has three hearts.
facts.explanation: Two pump blood through the gills, one pumps it around the body.

facts.text: Octopuses have bones in their arms.
facts.explanation: They have no bones at all, which lets them squeeze through tiny gaps.

facts.text: Sealed honey can stay edible for thousands of years.
facts.explanation: Its low moisture and acidity stop bacteria growing.

facts.text: Bees make honey from tree sap.
facts.explanation: Bees make honey from flower nectar.

facts.text: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
facts.explanation: Venus spins so slowly that one rotation takes longer than one orbit of the Sun.

facts.text: Mars is the hottest planet in the solar system.
facts.explanation: Venus is the hottest: its thick atmosphere traps heat.

facts.text: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.
facts.explanation: The Sun is about 150 million km away.

facts.text: The Moon produces its own light.
facts.explanation: Moonlight is sunlight reflected off the Moon's surface.

facts.text: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones.
facts.explanation: The count settles at 206 once growing bones have fused.

facts.text: Babies are born with fewer bones than adults.
facts.explanation: Babies have around 300 bones; many fuse together as they grow.

facts.text: Water boils at a lower temperature at high altitude.
facts.explanation: Lower air pressure lets water boil sooner, so cooking takes longer in the hills.

facts.text: Pure water is a good conductor of electricity.
facts.explanation: Pure water conducts poorly. Dissolved salts are what carry the current.

facts.text: Raja Harishchandra (1913) is considered India's first full-length feature film.
facts.explanation: It was made by Dadasaheb Phalke.

facts.text: Lagaan won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film.
facts.explanation: Lagaan was nominated in 2002 but did not win.

facts.text: 'Naatu Naatu' from RRR won the Oscar for Best Original Song.
facts.explanation: It won at the 2023 Academy Awards.

facts.text: 'Jai Ho' was first heard in the film Lagaan.
facts.explanation: 'Jai Ho' is from Slumdog Millionaire, where it won an Oscar.

facts.text: Chess is believed to have grown out of the Indian game chaturanga.
facts.explanation: Chaturanga was played in India around the 6th century.

facts.text: Viswanathan Anand never became world chess champion.
facts.explanation: Anand was world champion several times, including 2007 to 2013.

facts.text: Neeraj Chopra won Olympic gold in javelin at Tokyo 2020.
facts.explanation: It was India's first Olympic gold in athletics.

facts.text: India has never won an Olympic gold medal in hockey.
facts.explanation: India has won eight Olympic golds in men's hockey.

facts.text: Assam is one of the largest tea-growing regions in the world.
facts.explanation: Assam's Brahmaputra valley produces a large share of India's tea.

facts.text: Darjeeling tea is grown in Kerala.
facts.explanation: Darjeeling is in the hills of West Bengal.

facts.text: Chillies reached India from the Americas through Portuguese traders.
facts.explanation: They arrived in the 16th century and quickly took over Indian cooking.

facts.text: Potatoes are native to India.
facts.explanation: Potatoes come from the Andes in South America.

facts.text: Botanically, a banana is a berry.
facts.explanation: It develops from a single flower with one ovary, which makes it a berry.

facts.text: Botanically, a strawberry is a true berry.
facts.explanation: Strawberries are not true berries. Their seeds sit on the outside.

facts.text: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.
facts.explanation: It can sprint at around 100 km/h in short bursts.

facts.text: Cheetahs have never lived in India.
facts.explanation: Asiatic cheetahs once roamed India, and cheetahs were brought to Kuno National Park in 2022.

facts.text: Elephants are pregnant for almost two years.
facts.explanation: Pregnancy lasts around 22 months, the longest of any land animal.

facts.text: An elephant's pregnancy lasts about nine months, like a human's.
facts.explanation: It lasts around 22 months.

facts.text: Mount Everest sits on the border between Nepal and China.
facts.explanation: The summit ridge divides Nepal from Tibet.

facts.text: K2 is taller than Mount Everest.
facts.explanation: Everest is about 8,849 m; K2 is about 8,611 m.

facts.text: Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth.
facts.explanation: A desert is defined by low rainfall, and Antarctica gets very little.

facts.text: The Sahara is the coldest desert in the world.
facts.explanation: The Sahara is one of the hottest. Antarctica is the coldest.

facts.text: The Great Wall of China is thousands of kilometres long.
facts.explanation: All its sections together stretch over 20,000 km.

facts.text: The Great Wall of China is easy to see from the Moon with the naked eye.
facts.explanation: It is far too narrow to see from the Moon.

facts.text: Goldfish can remember things for months.
facts.explanation: They can be trained to respond to sounds and lights.

facts.text: Goldfish have a memory of only three seconds.
facts.explanation: That is a myth. Experiments show goldfish remember for months.

facts.text: A lightning bolt is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
facts.explanation: A bolt can heat the air to around 30,000 kelvin, about five times hotter than the Sun's surface.

facts.text: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
facts.explanation: Tall buildings like the Empire State Building are hit many times a year.

facts.text: Diamonds are made of carbon.
facts.explanation: They are carbon atoms locked in a very strong crystal structure.

facts.text: Diamonds form from squeezed coal.
facts.explanation: Most diamonds form from carbon deep in the Earth's mantle, not from coal.

facts.text: Indian Railways is one of the largest employers in the world.
facts.explanation: It employs over a million people.

facts.text: India's first passenger train ran from Delhi to Agra.
facts.explanation: It ran from Bombay's Bori Bunder to Thane in 1853.

facts.text: India's Constitution is the longest written national constitution in the world.
facts.explanation: It has hundreds of articles and many schedules.

facts.text: India became a republic on 15 August 1947.
facts.explanation: That was Independence Day. India became a republic on 26 January 1950.

facts.text: India's Constitution lists 22 scheduled languages.
facts.explanation: They are listed in the Eighth Schedule.

facts.text: English has no official status in India.
facts.explanation: English is an official language of the Union government alongside Hindi.

facts.text: The Indian mathematician Brahmagupta wrote rules for calculating with zero.
facts.explanation: He set them out in the 7th century.

facts.text: Aryabhata was a Mughal emperor.
facts.explanation: Aryabhata was a 5th-century mathematician and astronomer.

facts.text: International Day of Yoga is celebrated on 21 June.
facts.explanation: The UN declared it in 2014; 21 June is the longest day in the northern hemisphere.

facts.text: International Day of Yoga falls on 2 October.
facts.explanation: 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti. Yoga Day is 21 June.

facts.text: The first IPL season was played in 2008.
facts.explanation: Eight franchises took part.

facts.text: Chennai Super Kings won the first IPL.
facts.explanation: Rajasthan Royals won the first season in 2008.

facts.text: A football match has two halves of 45 minutes each.
facts.explanation: Stoppage time is added at the end of each half.

facts.text: Brazil has never won the FIFA World Cup.
facts.explanation: Brazil has won it five times, more than any other country.

facts.text: P. V. Sindhu has won two Olympic medals in badminton.
facts.explanation: Silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020.

facts.text: Badminton shuttlecocks are traditionally made with chicken feathers.
facts.explanation: Traditional shuttlecocks use goose or duck feathers.

facts.text: The same side of the Moon always faces Earth.
facts.explanation: The Moon spins once for every orbit, so we always see the same face.

facts.text: There is no gravity on the Moon.
facts.explanation: The Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's.

facts.text: Saturn is less dense than water.
facts.explanation: It is mostly hydrogen and helium.

facts.text: Saturn is the only planet with rings.
facts.explanation: Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune have rings too, just fainter ones.

facts.text: A human heart beats around 100,000 times a day.
facts.explanation: About 70 beats a minute adds up to roughly 100,000 a day.

facts.text: Humans use only 10% of their brains.
facts.explanation: Brain scans show we use virtually all of it.

facts.text: Our tongues can detect sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami.
facts.explanation: Umami is the savoury taste of foods like tomatoes and mushrooms.

facts.text: Each part of the tongue can taste only one flavour.
facts.explanation: The 'tongue map' is a myth. Every area can sense every taste.

facts.text: Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge ran at a Mumbai cinema for over 20 years.
facts.explanation: It played at Maratha Mandir from 1995 into the 2010s.

facts.text: Sholay was released in the 2000s.
facts.explanation: Sholay came out in 1975.

facts.text: Baahubali was shot in Telugu and Tamil at the same time.
facts.explanation: It was later dubbed into Hindi, Malayalam and other languages.

facts.text: Baahubali: The Beginning came out after Baahubali 2.
facts.explanation: The Beginning released in 2015, The Conclusion in 2017.

facts.text: A. R. Rahman won two Oscars for Slumdog Millionaire.
facts.explanation: Best Original Score and Best Original Song for 'Jai Ho'.

facts.text: Lata Mangeshkar never sang a film song.
facts.explanation: She recorded thousands of film songs over seven decades.

facts.text: Diwali is known as the festival of lights.
facts.explanation: Homes are lit with diyas and lamps.

facts.text: Holi is celebrated at the start of winter.
facts.explanation: Holi marks the arrival of spring.

facts.text: Kerala is known as 'God's Own Country'.
facts.explanation: It's the state's tourism slogan.

facts.text: Goa is India's largest state by area.
facts.explanation: Goa is the smallest state. Rajasthan is the largest.

facts.text: The mango is India's national fruit.
facts.explanation: India grows hundreds of varieties, from Alphonso to Langra.

facts.text: India grows very few mangoes.
facts.explanation: India is the world's largest producer of mangoes.

facts.text: Penguins are birds that cannot fly.
facts.explanation: Their wings have become flippers for swimming.

facts.text: Wild penguins live at the North Pole.
facts.explanation: Wild penguins live almost only in the Southern Hemisphere.

facts.text: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly.
facts.explanation: Flying squirrels only glide.

facts.text: Bats are completely blind.
facts.explanation: All bats can see. Many also use echolocation.

facts.text: Kabaddi is a contact sport that originated in India.
facts.explanation: It has been played across South Asia for centuries.

facts.text: Pro Kabaddi League matches are played on grass.
facts.explanation: Pro Kabaddi is played indoors on mats.

facts.text: The Summer Olympics are held every four years.
facts.explanation: Summer and Winter Games now alternate, two years apart.

facts.text: The modern Olympic Games began in 1950.
facts.explanation: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896.

facts.text: MS Dhoni captained India to the T20 World Cup, the ODI World Cup and the Champions Trophy.
facts.explanation: India won them in 2007, 2011 and 2013.

facts.text: MS Dhoni played for India as a fast bowler.
facts.explanation: Dhoni was a wicketkeeper-batter.

facts.text: Wimbledon is played on grass courts.
facts.explanation: It is the oldest tennis tournament in the world.

facts.text: The French Open is played on grass courts.
facts.explanation: It is played on red clay at Roland-Garros.

facts.text: The Elephant Whisperers won the Oscar for Best Documentary Short Film.
facts.explanation: It won at the 2023 Academy Awards.

facts.text: No Indian film has ever been nominated for an Oscar.
facts.explanation: Mother India, Salaam Bombay! and Lagaan were all nominated.

facts.text: Kishore Kumar was also a film actor and director.
facts.explanation: He starred in hits like Chalti Ka Naam Gaadi.

facts.text: Mohammed Rafi sang only in Hindi.
facts.explanation: Rafi recorded songs in many Indian languages.

facts.text: Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar for his life's work.
facts.explanation: He received it in 1992, shortly before he died.

facts.text: Satyajit Ray made his films mainly in Tamil.
facts.explanation: Ray made his films mainly in Bengali.

facts.text: The name 'Bollywood' blends Bombay and Hollywood.
facts.explanation: Bombay is the old name of Mumbai, home of the Hindi film industry.

facts.text: Bollywood is the only film industry in India.
facts.explanation: Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Bengali and other industries thrive too.

facts.text: Mickey Mouse first appeared on screen in 1928.
facts.explanation: His breakout film was Steamboat Willie.

facts.text: Mickey Mouse was created by Warner Bros.
facts.explanation: Walt Disney and Ub Iwerks created Mickey.

facts.text: The first email was sent in the early 1970s.
facts.explanation: Ray Tomlinson sent it in 1971 on ARPANET.

facts.text: The World Wide Web and the internet are the same thing.
facts.explanation: The web is one service that runs on the internet, like email.
